newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cuts discount rate to 6.25 pct from 6.75 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy cuts discount rate to 6.25 pct from 6.75 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Italy said on Friday it would cut the official discount rate to 6.25 percent from 6.75 percent.
The cut will take effect on Monday, a Bank of Italy statement said. The last change to the discount rate was on January 21, when it was reduced by 75 basis points.
The Bank's fixed term advances, or Lombard rate, was simultaneously cut to 7.75 percent from a previous 8.25 percent.

The central bank has now cut rates four times since July 1996. Preliminary CPI data for June from 11 Italian cities pointed to inflation falling to an annual rate of 1.4-1.5 percent from 1.6 percent in May, the lowest level for 28 years.
The rate cut will come as a relief to the government, which is desperate to lower the interest bill on its debt mountain.

The government estimates that it saves 20 trillion lire ($12 billion) a year in debt servicing costs for every percentage point fall in the discount rate, once the cut has fully worked its way into the system.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who has staked his political career on Italy being a member of the single European currency right from the January 1, 1999 planned start, has been saying for the last month that all conditions were in place for a reduction in interest rates.
